# Banner

Banner: a prominent message at the top of a page. No dismiss and no side stripe — the caller mounts and unmounts it, and meaning comes from the fill and the icon alone.

Also asked as: announcement, top of page, system message, outage.

**Import:** `import { Banner } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Banner/Banner.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Banner/Banner.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Warning, Danger, Announcement, WithoutIcon, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Banner/Banner.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.default` + `appearance.default` · exit `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Banner` for a condition that applies to the whole page, for as long as it
holds: scheduled maintenance, an outage, an account-wide notice. It has no
timeout and no dismiss, so only mount it while the condition is true.

For something that belongs to one part of the page and stays until resolved
or dismissed, use `SectionMessage`. For a confirmation that something already
happened and needs no reply, use `Flag`.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Warning | The default, cautionary form. Example: "Scheduled maintenance begins at 9:00 PM EST." |
| Danger | Something that needs immediate attention, such as an outage. |
| Announcement | A general notice with nothing wrong. No icon and no severity. |

## Motion

Banner reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | Pushes the page down, then fades in. |
| exit | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades, then the page closes the gap. |

## Best practices

### Use the danger banner only when action is needed now. {#use-the-danger-banner-only-when-action-is-needed-now}

Routine news belongs in an announcement.

Do: Danger for a canceled session.
Don't: Danger for a feature announcement.

### Show one banner at a time. {#show-one-banner-at-a-time}

Stacked banners compete and push the page down.

Do: A single announcement.
Don't: A warning and a danger banner stacked.

### Keep it to one line. {#keep-it-to-one-line}

A banner is read at a glance; long copy belongs on the page.

Do: One short sentence.
Don't: A paragraph in the banner.

## Accessibility

- **Announced as a status.** The banner's role is `status`, so assistive
  technology reports its content without interrupting the current task.
- **Severity needs more than color.** `warning` and `danger` pair their fill
  with a leading icon, but the icon is decorative, so say the severity in the
  words of the message. Only `announcement` relies on fill alone, which suits
  a notice with no severity.
- **No focus trap.** A banner never captures focus or keyboard navigation; it
  sits in the page's reading order like any other content.
- **A banner link takes focus like any link.** It shows the 2px focus ring and
  its text names the destination.

## Related

- For a message scoped to one region of the page, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a timed confirmation that something already happened, use `Flag`.
- For a short note tied to one object on the page, use `InlineMessage`.

Same group: `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `Modal` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Icon.** Leading glyph for `warning` and `danger`; `announcement` has none.
2. **Message.** Short text that fits on one line. A link inside inherits the banner's text color and is underlined, so it stays visible on every fill.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Fill and text per appearance. |
| Hovered | Not a control, so nothing changes. |
| Pressed | Nothing changes; there is no pressed layer. |
| Focused | Tab skips the banner; a link inside shows the 2px focus ring. |
| Disabled | Not supported. Unmount the banner once the condition clears. |
| Truncated | Not supported. Keep the message short enough to fit. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Warning | `--ds-background-warning`, `--ds-text-warning`, `--ds-icon-warning` |
| Danger | `--ds-background-danger`, `--ds-text-danger`, `--ds-icon-danger` |
| Announcement | `--ds-background-neutral`, `--ds-text` |
| Message | `--body-default`; a link at `--type-weight-medium` |
| Padding, gap | `--pad-y-md`, `--pad-x-md`, `--inline-md` |
| Icon | `--icon-md` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use concise, scannable language that states the problem. | Write a long message; there is no way to expand it. |
| Say the severity, what is affected and what to do. | Leave out what the person should do next. |
| Own the problem when it is ours: "We lost the connection." | Blame the person: "Something is wrong with your connection." |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `appearance` | enum | `'warning'` | `warning` (default form), `danger` (critical, needs immediate attention) or `announcement` (general, no icon). |
| `icon` | string or node or enum | — | A Font Awesome Free solid glyph name or a node. `false` removes the appearance's default icon. |
| `children` | node (required) | — | Message content. Typically text, optionally with a link. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |
